steps.npc: Hello there. I am Gerardus, master cartographer. Do you have any charts of the ocean you would be willing to share with me?

options.text: Yes, have a look at my charts...

steps.player: Yes, have a look at my charts...

steps.text: If the player doesn't have their captain's log:

steps.npc: You... don't appear to have any with you.

steps.player: Oh, let me go and fetch my captain's log.

steps.text: If the player has charts to show him:
You show your charts to Gerardus.

steps.npc: Yes, these are some fantastic charts! Please, accept these...

steps.text: For completely charting the Northern Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a book about lighthouses?
For completely charting the Unquiet Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a burned key?
For completely charting the Shrouded Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a weird black orb?
For completely charting the Ardent Ocean, Gerardus hands you... a bedsheet?

steps.player: ... What am I meant to do with these?

steps.npc: I'm not sure, but you seem like a smart person. I'm sure you'll figure something out.

steps.text: If the player has nothing new to show him:

steps.npc: Hmm... these are indeed nice charts, but I'm afraid you've shown me all of these already.

options.text: Do you have any spare trinkets?
options.condition: After previously receiving any item from him:

steps.player: Do you have any spare trinkets?

steps.text: If the player still has any items received from Gerardus or has used them all to get paint:

steps.npc: Well, I do have plenty of trinkets, but I suspect you've gotten all the use out of anything I could give you.

steps.text: If the player is missing any items they haven't used to get paint:
Gerardus hands you another book about lighthouses. You get the feeling he might have had too many of them in the first place.

steps.npc: Well, over the years, while out mapping the world, I have amassed a collection of.... rare and valuable items.
My maps are now only a few seas from completion. If you're able to help me, I will make sure you are well rewarded for your troubles. So, what do you say?
